title: lock: stop fingerprint scans while the display is blanked
author: slr01
body:
## What and why

While a display is blanked, the lock screen keeps the fingerprint reader running scan cycles against an empty pad. On fingerprint readers that thermally self-disable (Broadcom CV3 / `0a5c:5843`, Goodix `27c6:533c`, Elan `04f3:0c4b`, all `libfprint-tod`), that cycles the driver into `Device disabled to prevent overheating` refusals: 31,534 `PAM_AUTHINFO_UNAVAIL` / code 9 returns in under four hours on a CV3, in a 205 s-refusing / 122 s-available cycle. Each refusal re-arms the 250 ms retry timer, so the reader stays in the storm.

This PR stops new scans while the display is blanked and re-arms on wake. With it, a CV3 logged **0 refusals across a 15-minute lock** and read on the first touch after wake ([measurement thread](/omacom/omarchy/pull/12201#issuecomment-5721534266)).

## Changes (3 lines-worth of gating, purely additive vs stock)

- `runBlank()`: stop `fingerprintRetryTimer` so a blanked display is not re-arming scan cycles
- `startFingerprint()`: return early while `displaysBlank`
- `runWake()`: re-arm a scan if a lock is active

No `abort()`: an in-flight scan is allowed to finish; on readers where `power/wakeup` is disabled, the reader cannot wake the compositor, so aborting on blank can strand it with nothing to re-arm it.

## Notes

- Composes with the libfprint temperature/backoff model in libfprint#7179 rather than colliding with it.
- Purely additive against `quattro`; no behavior change while the display is awake.
